To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intracellular retention and processing of TI antigens can have a significant impact on antigen presentation to T cells by APC, and that the inhibition of antigen processing and presentation is dependent on the chemical nature of TI antigens.
the intracellular accumulation of complex carbohydrates derived from pathogens is a common phenomenon that is responsible for the impairment of antigen presentation to T cells by APC.
the intracellular retention in APC of TI antigens derived from pathogenic parasites, which are not removed by the host cell, can interfere with the presentation of TD antigens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the consequences of the intracelluar retention of TI antigens on the presentation of TD antigens to T cells.
understanding the molecular mechanisms by which intracellular pathogens can be recognized by the immune system.
the study of the mechanisms by which the host can recognize and eliminate pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intracellular retention and/or accumulation of complex carbohydrate antigens derived from intracellular pathogens is not a general rule and that there are no general mechanisms for the inhibition of antigen processing and/or presentation.
the intracellular accumulation of complex polysaccharide TI antigens does not impair antigen presentation by APC.
, in general, the presence of TI antigens in APC does not impair the presentation of TD antigens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intracellular retention time of TI antigens is a critical factor in the processing and antigen presentation to specific T cells of TD antigens.
the intracellular retention time of a pathogen-derived TI antigen in an APC can be a major determinant of the efficiency of antigen presentation to specific T cells.
intracellular pathogens are able to modulate their antigen presentation to T cells by means of the intracellular accumulation of TI antigens.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the intracellular retention and processing of TI antigens derived from pathogenic bacteria or fungi, and even from the normal turnover of host tissues, may be a major cause of the impairment of T-cell-dependent immunity to TD antigens.
the intracellular retention period of a TI antigen is a key factor in determining whether the TI antigen will impair or enhance the antigen presentation to T cells by APC.
the intracellular retention and degradation of TI antigens can have important consequences on the processing of TD antigens.
